x: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate
Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted, Majestic One, whose names are sanctified:
God has heard the speech of her who disputes with you about her husband and complains to God, and God hears your exchange; indeed God is Hearing, Seeing (1)
The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ:
the speech of her who disputes with you about her husband
. The woman who was disputing with the Messenger of God ﷺ about her husband was a woman of the Anṣār.
The people of knowledge differed about her lineage and her name.
Some of them said: Khawla bint Thaʿlaba.
Some of them said: Her name is Khuwayla bint Thaʿlaba.
Others said: She is Khuwayla bint Khuwaylid.
Others said: She is Khuwayla bint al-Ṣāmit.
Others said: She is Khuwayla bint al-Dulayj.

Her disputing with the Messenger of God ﷺ about her husband — her husband being Aws b. al-Ṣāmit — consisted of her going back and forth with him ⁽¹⁾ over his affair, and what he had said to her: "You are to me like my mother's back," and her conversing with him about that. This is what the people of interpretation said, and the transmission is replete with it.
Mention of those who said that, and of the reports that came regarding it:

Then she said: "O Messenger of God, my companionship has grown long, and I have shaken out my belly for him." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "You have become forbidden to him." And whenever he said to her, "You have become forbidden to him," she cried out and said: "I complain to God of my want." He said: Then revelation came down — ʿĀʾisha had risen to wash the other side of his head — and ʿĀʾisha motioned to her to be quiet. She said: When revelation came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, something like drowsiness would take hold of him; and when the revelation was completed he said: "Call your husband." She went back and forth with the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly ⁽³⁾, then said: "O God, I complain to You today of the hardship of my state and my loneliness, and of how hard separation from him is for me. Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against God. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever (17)

The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, says: Their wealth will not avail these hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, so that they might ransom themselves with it from God's humiliating punishment of them; nor their children, so that they might help them and rescue them from God when He punishes them.
Those are the companions of the Fire
. He says: These who took as allies a people with whom God is angry — and they are the hypocrites —
are the companions of the Fire
, meaning: its people, those who [are its people] ⁽¹⁾;
. He says: they will remain in the Fire without end.
Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted:
On the Day when God will resurrect them all, then they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars (18)
The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, says: These whom God mentioned ⁽²⁾ are the companions of the Fire, on the day when God resurrects them all. So "on the day" (
. What is meant by His words
On the Day when God will resurrect them all
is: [on the day when God resurrects them all] ⁽³⁾ from their graves, alive, in the form ⁽⁴⁾ they had before their death, and they swear to Him as they swear to you, lying and acting falsely in it.

c: As Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda,
m: then they will swear to Him
. He said: The hypocrite will swear to Him on the Day of Resurrection as he swore to His friends in this world ⁽¹⁾.

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: On the Day when God will resurrect them all
, the verse: By God, the hypocrites will swear to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection just as they swore to His friends in this world.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Simāk b.
m: Ḥarb al-Bakrī, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was in the shade ⁽²⁾ of a room, and the shade was about to recede from him, and he said: "A man will come to you" — or: "a man will appear" — "with the eye ⁽³⁾ of a devil, so do not speak to him." It was not long before he came and looked in, and behold, a blue-eyed man; and he (the Prophet) said to him: "On what account do you revile me, you and so-and-so [and so-and-so] ⁽⁴⁾?" He said: He went and called his companions, and they swore that they had not done (it). Then was revealed:
On the Day when God will resurrect them all, then they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars

x: and they will think that they are upon something
. He says: They suppose that in their oaths and their swearing by God — (oaths which are) lies — they are upon something of truth;
Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars
Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted:
Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of God. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers (19)
The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, means by His words
Satan has gained mastery over them
: Satan overcame them, and made them forget the remembrance of God;
Those are the party of Satan
, meaning his soldiers and his followers;
Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers
. He says: Unquestionably, the soldiers of Satan and his followers are the ones who perish, cheated in their bargain.
Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted:
Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger — those will be among the most humiliated (20). God has written: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, God is Strong, Mighty (21)

The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, says: Those who contradict God and His Messenger regarding His bounds, and regarding what He made obligatory upon them ⁽¹⁾ of His obligations, and so are hostile to Him.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger
. He says: They are hostile to God and His Messenger.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda,
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, saying: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan told us, saying: Waraqāʾ told us
m: — both together from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words:
. He said: They are hostile; they are in opposition (

x: those will be among the most humiliated
. The Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, says: These who oppose God and His Messenger are among the people of abasement; for victory belongs to God and His Messenger.
God has written: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers."
He says: God decreed, and inscribed in the Mother of the Book: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers, over whoever opposes Me and contends against Me."
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: God has written: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"
, the verse. He said: God wrote a writing and enforced it ⁽¹⁾.

x: . He says: Indeed God, Mighty is His praise, is possessed of strength and power over everyone who opposes Him and His Messenger, (power) to destroy him; and possessed of might, so that no one is able to gain victory over Him when He destroys that person's ally, or punishes him, or afflicts him personally with harm.
Discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted:

You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their clan. Those — He has written faith in their hearts and supported them with a spirit from Him; and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of God. Unquestionably, the party of God are the successful (22)
He, Mighty is His praise, means by His words:
You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger

: You will not find, O Muḥammad, a people who affirm God and acknowledge the Last Day loving those who are hostile ⁽²⁾ to God and His Messenger and are in opposition to the two of them, and who contradict the command of God and His prohibition;
even if they were their fathers

. He says: even if those who opposed God and His Messenger were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their clan. God, Mighty is His praise, informed His Prophet ﷺ by this verse that those who took as allies a people with whom God is angry are not among the people of faith in God or in the Last Day; and that is why they took as allies those whom they took as allies among the Jews.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger
— that is: whoever is hostile to God and His Messenger ⁽¹⁾.

x: Those — He has written faith in their hearts

. He, Mighty is His praise, says: These who do not love those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their clan — God has written faith in their hearts. What is meant by that is: He has decreed faith for their hearts. So "in" (

); and the Exalted One, may His mention be exalted, informed us that He wrote faith in their hearts for them. And since faith is a matter of the hearts, and it was known from the report about the hearts that what is meant by them is their owners, mention of them (the hearts) sufficed in place of mentioning their owners.
and supported them with a spirit from Him
. He says: And He strengthened them with a proof from Him, and light and guidance;
and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow
. He says: And He will admit them to orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow;
. He says: remaining in them forever;
because of their obedience to Him in this world,
and they are pleased with Him
in the Hereafter, because of His admitting them to Paradise;
Those are the party of God
. He says: Those whose description this is are God's soldiers and His friends;
. He says: Unquestionably, God's soldiers and His friends
. He says: They are the abiding, the prosperous, who attain what they sought and desired, through their toil ⁽¹⁾ in this world and their obedience to their Lord.

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في السنة (592)، والآجري في الشريعة (655)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (909)، والاعتقاد من طريق نوح بن ميمون به.

notes.en: See *al-Nashr* 2/287.
notes.ar: ينظر النشر 2/ 287.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 184 إلى ابن المنذر، وذكره الواحدي في أسباب النزول ص 306.

notes.en: This is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Jaʿfar, Yaʿqūb in the transmission of Rawḥ, and Khalaf. See *al-Nashr* 2/288.
notes.ar: هي قراءة نافع وابن كثير وأبي عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي وأبي جعفر ويعقوب في رواية روح وخلف. ينظر النشر 2/ 288.

notes.en: Yaʿqūb also read it thus in the transmission of Ruways. See *al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ* 8/236.
notes.ar: وبها قرأ يعقوب في رواية رويس. ينظر البحر المحيط 8/ 236.

notes.ar: في م: "عليك".

notes.ar: أخرجه الواحدي في أسباب النزول ص 307 من طريق جرير به. وأخرجه أحمد 6/ 229 (الميمنية)، ومسلم (2165/ 11)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11571)، والبيهقي في الشعب (9098) من طريق الأعمش به.

notes.en: Thus in the copies. The author of *al-Lisān* said: *al-sāmma* is death, a rare (form); the well-known (form) is *al-sām*, with a light *mīm* and no *hāʾ*. *Lisān* (s-m-m).
notes.ar: كذا في النسخ، قال صاحب اللسان: السامَّة: الموت، نادر، والمعروف "السامُ" بتخفيف الميم بلا هاء. اللسان (س م م).

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2/279 and in the *Muṣannaf* (19460); Aḥmad 6/199 (*al-Maymaniyya*); ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd (1469); al-Bukhārī (6395); Muslim (2165/10); al-Nasāʾī in *al-Kubrā* (10215); Ibn Ḥibbān (6441); and al-Bayhaqī 9/203 — via Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha. It was also transmitted by al-Ḥumaydī (248); Aḥmad 6/37 and 85 (*al-Maymaniyya*); al-Bukhārī (6024, 6256, 6927); Muslim (2165/10); al-Tirmidhī (2701); al-Nasāʾī in *al-Kubrā* (10213, 10214, 10216, 11572); and Ibn Māja (3689) — via al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/184, attributed it to Saʿīd b. Manṣūr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 279، وفي المصنف (19460)، وأحمد 6/ 199 (الميمنية)، وعبد بن حميد (1469)، والبخاري (6395)، ومسلم (2165/ 10)، والنسائي في الكبرى (10215)، وابن حبان (6441)، والبيهقي 9/ 203 من طريق معمر عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة. وأخرجه الحميدي (248)، وأحمد 6/ 37، 85 (الميمنية)، والبخاري (6024، 6256، 6927)، ومسلم (2165/ 10)، والترمذي (2701)، والنسائي في الكبرى (10213، 10214، 10216، 11572)، وابن ماجه (3689) من طريق الزهري عن عروة، عن عائشة، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 184 إلى سعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted it (503) via Yazīd b. Zurayʿ. It was transmitted by Ibn Abī Shayba 8/442 — and via him Ibn Māja (3697) — and by al-Bazzār (2010 — *Kashf*) via Saʿīd. ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd transmitted it — as in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/184 — and from him al-Tirmidhī (3301), Muslim (2163/7), Abū Dāwūd (5207), and al-Wāḥidī in *Asbāb al-nuzūl*, p. 307, via Qatāda. Aḥmad 19/14 (11948), al-Bukhārī (6258) and Muslim (2163) transmitted it via ʿUbayd Allāh b. Abī Bakr from Anas.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن حبان (503) من طريق يزيد بن زريع به. وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 8/ 442 - ومن طريقه ابن ماجه (3697) - والبزار (2010 - كشف) من طريق سعيد به. وأخرجه عبد بن حميد - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 184 - وعنه الترمذي (3301)، ومسلم (2163/ 7)، وأبو داود (5207)، والواحدي في أسباب النزول ص 307 من طريق قتادة به، وأخرجه أحمد 19/ 14 (11948)، والبخاري (6258)، ومسلم (2163) من طريق عبيد الله بن أبي بكر عن أنس.

notes.en: Mentioned by al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr 17/299 and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 8/74.
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 17/ 299، وابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 74.

notes.en: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read with *ḍamma* on the *shīn* and, when beginning (with the word), with *ḍamma* on the *alif*; the rest read with *kasra* on the *shīn* and, when beginning, with *kasra* on the *alif*. *al-Kashf* 2/315.
notes.ar: قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر بضم الشين والابتداء بضم الألف، وقرأ الباقون بكسر الشين والابتداء بكسر الألف. الكشف 2/ 315.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "أي".

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it in *al-Zuhd*, p. 240, via Saʿīd. Ibn Saʿd (*al-Ṭabaqāt* 7/142), al-Fasawī (*al-Maʿrifa wa-l-tārīkh* 2/82) and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr (*Jāmiʿ bayān al-ʿilm wa-faḍlihi* 1/116 [104]) transmitted it via Qatāda.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد في الزهد ص 240 من طريق سعيد به. وأخرجه ابن سعد في الطبقات 7/ 142، والفسوي في المعرفة والتاريخ 2/ 82، وابن عبد البر في جامع بيان العلم وفضله 1/ 116 (104) من طريق قتادة به.

notes.en: Thus in the copies; perhaps the correct (name) is Muṭarrif b. ʿAbd Allāh, as in the source of the *takhrīj*.
notes.ar: كذا في النسخ. ولعل الصواب مطرف بن عبد الله كما في مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it in *al-Zuhd*, p. 240, via Saʿīd.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد في الزهد ص 240 من طريق سعيد به.

notes.en: *Tafsīr Mujāhid*, p. 651. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2/280 — and via him Ibn al-Jawzī in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, p. 480 — via Sulaymān al-Aḥwal from Mujāhid. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/185, attributed it to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 651. وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 280 - ومن طريقه ابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 480 - من طريق سليمان الأحول عن مجاهد. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 185 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it in his *Nāsikh*, p. 373, and Ibn Abī Shayba 12/81, from Ibn Idrīs. Isḥāq b. Rāhwayh transmitted it — as in *al-Maṭālib al-ʿāliya* (4140) — and Ibn al-Jawzī in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, p. 479, via Layth. Al-Ḥākim 2/482 transmitted it via Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/185, attributed it to Saʿīd b. Manṣūr, ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو عبيد في ناسخه ص 373، وابن أبي شيبة 12/ 81 عن ابن إدريس به. وأخرجه إسحاق بن راهويه - كما في المطالب العالية (4140) - وابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 479 من طريق ليث به. وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 482 من طريق مجاهد عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن علي بن أبي طالب. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 185 إلى سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: "*Aḥfā fulānan*": he pressed him in questioning and wore him out. *al-Wasīṭ* (ḥ-f-y).
notes.ar: أحفى فلانا: ألح عليه في السؤال وجَهَده. الوسيط (ح ف ى).

notes.en: In Ṣ, T2, T3: "*fa-ʿaẓẓamahum*"; in M: "*fa-waʿaẓahum*"; in T1: "*fa-ʿaṣamahum*." The adopted reading is from Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr. "He put a stop to them with the verse" (*qaṭaʿahum bi-l-āya*) means: He made them desist from questioning.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "فعظمهم"، وفي م: "فوعظهم"، وفي ت 1: "فعصمهم". والمثبت من تفسير ابن كثير، وقطعهم بالآية: أي جعلهم يكفون عن المسألة.

notes.en: Mentioned by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 8/76.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 76.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2/280 — and via him Ibn al-Jawzī in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, p. 480 — from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 280 - ومن طريقه ابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 480 - عن معمر به.

notes.en: Ibn al-Jawzī transmitted it in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, pp. 480–481, via Muḥammad b. Saʿd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 480، 481 من طريق محمد بن سعد به.

notes.en: In the copies: "*ṣabara*" (was patient), which is a corruption; the adopted reading is from the source of the *takhrīj*.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "صبر"، وهو تحريف، والمثبت من مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: Al-Zaylaʿī mentioned it in *Takhrīj al-Kashshāf* 3/430 from the author (al-Ṭabarī). Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it in his *Nāsikh*, p. 371, and Ibn Mardawayh — as in al-Zaylaʿī's *Takhrīj al-Kashshāf* 3/430 — via Abū Ṣāliḥ. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/185, attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره الزيلعي في تخريج الكشاف 3/ 430 عن المصنف، وأخرجه أبو عبيد في ناسخه ص 371، وابن مردويه - كما في تخريج الكشاف للزيلعي 3/ 430 - من طريق أبي صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 185 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In M: "God lightened."
notes.ar: في م: "خفف الله".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba 12/81, ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd (90), al-Tirmidhī (3300), al-Bazzār (668), al-Nasāʾī in *Khaṣāʾiṣ ʿAlī* (152), Abū Yaʿlā (400), Ibn Ḥibbān (6941, 6942), al-Naḥḥās in his *Nāsikh*, p. 701, and Ibn al-Jawzī in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, p. 478, transmitted it via Sufyān al-Thawrī. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/185, attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 12/ 81، وعبد بن حميد (90)، والترمذي (3300)، والبزار (668)، والنسائي في خصائص على (152)، وأبو يعلى (400)، وابن حبان (6941، 6942) والنحاس في ناسخه ص 701، وابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 478 من طريق سفيان الثوري به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 185 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Thus in Ṣ, M, T1; in T2, T3: "*al-ḥanth*" (the breaking of an oath). Perhaps what is meant by "the wicked one" (*al-khabīth*) is Satan, and God knows best.
notes.ar: كذا في ص، م، ت 1. وفي ت 2، ت 3: "الحنث" ولعل المراد بالخبيث الشيطان، والله أعلم.

notes.en: Mentioned by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 8/76. Ibn al-Jawzī transmitted, in *Nawāsikh al-Qurʾān*, p. 479, via ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, from his father, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, something similar.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 76. وأخرج ابن الجوزي في نواسخ القرآن ص 479 من طريق علي بن الحسين عن أبيه عن يزيد عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس نحوه.

notes.en: In T2, T3: "your conferring" (*munājātikum*).
notes.ar: في ت 2، ت 3: "مناجاتكم".

notes.en: *Tafsīr Mujāhid*, p. 651.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 651.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2/280 from Maʿmar. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/186, attributed it to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 280 عن معمر به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 186 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: In M: "together" (*maʿan*).
notes.ar: في م: "معا".

notes.en: In M: "walls" (*judur*, plural). The disagreement about this reading will be mentioned in Sūrat al-Ḥashr.
notes.ar: في م: "جدر". وسيأتي ذكر الاختلاف في هذه القراءة في سورة الحشر.

notes.en: Al-Bazzār transmitted it (2270 — *Kashf*) from Ibn al-Muthannā. Aḥmad 4/48 (2147) and al-Ṭabarānī (12309) transmitted it via Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar. Aḥmad 4/231–232 and 5/316 (2407, 2408, 3277), al-Ḥākim 2/482, al-Bayhaqī in *al-Dalāʾil* 5/282, and al-Wāḥidī in *Asbāb al-nuzūl*, p. 309, (transmitted it); and likewise Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr and Ibn Mardawayh — as in al-Zaylaʿī's *Takhrīj al-Kashshāf* 3/432 — via Simāk, with similar wording. Al-Suyūṭī, in *al-Durr al-manthūr* 6/186, attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه البزار (2270 - كشف) عن ابن المثنى به. وأخرجه أحمد 4/ 48 (2147)، والطبراني (12309) من طريق محمد بن جعفر به. وأخرجه أحمد 4/ 231، 232، 5/ 316 (2407، 2408، 3277) والحاكم 2/ 482، والبيهقي في الدلائل 5/ 282، والواحدي في أسباب النزول ص 309، وأخرجه كذلك ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره، وابن مردويه - كما في تخريج الكشاف للزيلعي 3/ 432 من طريق سماك بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 186 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.ar: في م: "ببيعتهم".
